criteria.text: Identifies that Section 2.2 of the Supply Agreement renews the agreement automatically for successive five-year Renewal Terms, and that non-renewal requires notice given no more than 270 and no less than 240 days before expiry. Explains that this is effectively a 30-day window and that missing it locks Harrowgate into five more years.

Identifies that Section 3.1 of the Supply Agreement requires Harrowgate to buy all glass and PET containers for any beverage product, worldwide, exclusively from Veltmar. Explains that this goes well beyond the term sheet's agreed scope of amber glass bottles for beer brands at U.S. and Canadian facilities, and that Harrowgate is bound by the broader executed text.

Identifies that Recital C of Amendment No. 1 records receipt of the 14% Price Adjustment Notice on August 3, 2026. Explains that the 30-day objection period under Supply Agreement Section 5.4 expired on or about September 2, 2026, before the amendment's September 21, 2026 date, so the increase is deemed accepted absent an express extension or waiver.

Identifies that Section 2 of Amendment No. 1 replaces Supply Agreement Section 11.2, removing product recall costs from the carve-outs to the liability cap and limiting the indemnity carve-out to third-party intellectual property claims. Explains that recall and product-liability exposure is now capped at six months of fees.

Identifies that Section 4 of Amendment No. 1 adds a new Section 14.4 that lets Veltmar assign without Harrowgate's consent to Affiliates or to successors by merger, change of control or sale of business, overriding Section 14.3. Explains that nothing prevents assignment to a competitor and that Harrowgate remains bound by the consent requirement, so the restriction is now one-sided.
States that under Supply Agreement Section 15.2 written amendments take precedence over the Supply Agreement, so Amendment No. 1 controls where it conflicts with the Supply Agreement.
States that the liability cap in Supply Agreement Section 11.1 equals the fees paid by Customer in the six months before the claim arose.
Is organized as a memo addressed to the supervising partner, with issues listed item by item. Each item gives the document and section where the issue appears and a recommended fix.

For at least one issue whose fix requires new or revised drafting, proposes specific contract language, such as a restored Section 11.2, a narrowed Section 3.1, a revised renewal clause, or a competitor exclusion for assignment.

Fails if the response concludes that Harrowgate can still timely object to the 14% price increase under Section 5.4 without obtaining an extension or waiver, or treats the objection window as still open as of the amendment date.
Fails if the response concludes that the term sheet's narrower exclusivity scope governs or binds the parties over Supply Agreement Section 3.1.
